title: AlphaDirection1: EEG, ECG, PPG in the resting state and working memory for sequentially and simultaneously presented digits
description: Raw 64-channel EEG, ECG, PPG and behavioral recordings from 30 healthy young adults during resting state and a visual verbal working memory (digit span) task with serial recall. Digit sequences of seven items were presented either simultaneously or sequentially at different rates and with different delays, allowing examination of how temporal presentation structure affects neural oscillations, especially alpha activity. The dataset supports work on working memory load classification, ERP and oscillation analyses, and links between neural, peripheral physiological and behavioral measures.
methods_description: Resting-state session: four alternating 1-minute eyes-closed and eyes-open blocks, followed by about 4 minutes of passive cartoon watching. Working memory task: participants viewed seven-digit sequences under four presentation modes (simultaneous 2800 ms; fast sequential 400 ms per digit; fast sequential with 600 ms ISI; slow sequential 1000 ms per digit) and typed the digits in serial order on a numpad. EEG, ECG and PPG were recorded in BrainVision format, with trial-wise accuracy and partial-score behavioral measures.
